rule: Both arms measured against SPY, not just each other, and BOTH arms adjusted for contributed capital IN THE EXPERIMENT WINDOW only. ARM B: return = current total_value - rh_deposits.json experiment_window.adjusted_basis. Do NOT use total_contributed_capital: it measures from the bot's 2026-07-23 inception, a different window, and it charges ~$165 of pre-window deposits against in-window gains. On 2026-09-01 the two methods disagreed in SIGN (+1.1% vs -1.5%). ARM A: return = current equity - arm_A.start_equity, but FIRST read status.json capital_flow.state. clean = no adjustment needed. contaminated = subtract capital_flow.net first. unknown = the check failed ON THIS RUN. status.json is REWRITTEN every run, so one timeout or 500 overwrites a clean reading and destroys the evidence. Do NOT read unknown as clean, and do NOT discard earlier evidence: WALK status.json HISTORY for the most recent run reporting clean or contaminated -- `for c in $(git log --format=%h -200 -- status.json); do git show $c:status.json; done` -- the same technique audit-prompt.md L49 prescribes for earnings_guard, which is the identical field shape with the identical failure. Report using that reading and name its checked_at plus the gap: 'clean as of <checked_at>, unchecked for N days', which is a BOUNDED uncertainty. Only if NO clean/contaminated reading exists inside the window is the basis genuinely unverified, and even then report the comparison flagged PROVISIONAL rather than withholding it: 2026-11-24 is a scheduled decision and silence is not a safer answer than a caveated one. (Reworded 2026-09-01 on Devon's explicit approval. The previous rule named only Arm B and pointed at the inception total, so a cold reader following it landed on the wrong window for one arm and no capital check at all for the other.)
design_principle: Match the strategy to the platform's execution reliability. Stops need minutes; buy-and-hold tolerates hours. So the hybrid lives where execution is a solved problem.

config_history.note: The crypto 5% NEVER TRADED. Alpaca does not offer crypto in Colorado, so every crypto order was rejected on entitlement and that 5% sat in cash for the whole period.

Devon reallocated the dead crypto 5% into the active TRADING sleeve. Deployed TARGET is unchanged at 95% with a 5% cash buffer; what changed is that the 5% can now actually be deployed. Chose trade over hold because the hold sleeve was already unfilled at its 25% target, so adding room there would have parked the same cash twice.

arm_A.known_confound: Between 2026-08-24 and 2026-08-26 Arm A ran ~65% deployed against a ~100% deployed Arm B: 5 points dead crypto plus an unfilled hold sleeve. Any underperformance in that window is partly a DEPLOYMENT effect, not a strategy effect. The crypto half is fixed as of 08-26; the hold half is being measured via HOLD-GATE logging (commit 0f14492) rather than guessed at. SEPARATELY, a MEASUREMENT FIDELITY ASYMMETRY between the arms (laptop, 2026-09-01): Arm B detects contributed capital on EVERY reconcile pass via a rising edge on the broker's pending_deposits, writing an event and recomputing totals. Arm A had no deposit handling at all until 2026-09-01 and now checks /v2/account/activities once per cycle, publishing status.json capital_flow {state, net, events, checked_at}. Verified 2026-09-01: state=clean, $0.00 moved since 2026-08-24, and the detector was FALSIFIED by widening the window to 2026-01-01, where it correctly reported the account's original $250.00 CSD of 2026-06-08 - so the zero is a real result and not a broken check. The arms are now both continuous, but Arm A's history before 2026-09-01 rests on that single verified snapshot rather than on per-pass detection.
arm_A.downtime:
MEASURED 2026-10-08 (cloud; arm_a_downtime.py and tests/test_arm_a_downtime.py), added at Devon's say-so so that Arm A does not read as zero by omission: until now only Arm B had a downtime field. METHOD: from GitHub Actions run history, minutes of the 09:45-15:55 ET window (MARKET_HOLIDAYS excluded; the same window and calendar as arm_B.downtime_asymmetry) with a SUCCESSFUL Arm A run in progress. A failed or cancelled run does not count: the 2026-10-05 15:30 and 15:45 ET runs both ended failure after 15 minutes and Arm A had no stop checks from about 15:26 to the close. Arm A's stop-losses are evaluated only inside a run (60-second protective loop, no broker-side stops), so a minute with no run in progress is a minute nothing was watching. 2026-08-24 to 2026-10-08 15:00 ET (32.9 sessions, 12155 trading minutes): a run was in progress 70.3%; 28.3% was the built-in 15-minute trigger spacing (about 4.5 minutes of every 15, gaps of 10 minutes or less); UNPLANNED gaps (a lost run, a queue stall, a GitHub incident) were 174 minutes = 1.4%, in 10 episodes (08-26 34 and 14 min, 09-01 11, 09-09 12, 09-23 11, 09-28 13 and 14, 10-05 28 from 15:26 to the close, 10-07 19 and 18). Since 2026-09-22 11:01 alone: 103 minutes = 2.2%. 

HOW TO COMPARE IT WITH ARM B: the UNPLANNED figure is the like-for-like one. Arm A's 28.3% cadence is by design and Arm B has no equivalent (its daemon runs a pass every 60 seconds; its heartbeat spacing is only how often it pushes), so do NOT set 28.3% against Arm B's figure; Arm B's own edge minutes are the same kind of artifact and are excluded from its headline. Same span: Arm B 19.5% (21.8% with its edge minutes) against Arm A 1.4% unplanned. LIMITS: a proxy (a successful run is assumed to have run its protective passes; it cannot see a run that succeeded but whose state push was lost), and it measures when Arm A was unwatched, not what that cost. Both arms' cost per blind minute depends on whether anything needed doing there, and Arm B holds index ETFs with no stops.

arm_B.downtime_asymmetry:
SUPERSEDED FIGURE, read this first: an earlier version of this field said Arm B lost 160 market-minutes (~11 min/session). That was WRONG BY ~90% and in the UNSAFE direction. It counted only NO-PUSH gaps. During Claude session-limit and expired-login outages the laptop daemon stays alive and keeps pushing rh_status.json marked degraded=broker_unreachable, so a push-based measure scored every one of those minutes as UP. laptop proved it from this file's own arithmetic on 2026-09-17: 160 = 79 + 81 left no room for the 91-min 09-01 outage that happened inside the same window. The caveat here used to say the method OVER-reports, which was true of the minor case and false of the dominant one. 

CORRECTED FIGURE, 2026-08-24 to 2026-09-22, measured on the bot's ACTUAL trading window 09:45-15:55 ET, using the bot's own MARKET_HOLIDAYS calendar: 1484 blind market-minutes (24.7h) = 19.8% of trading time. Two DISJOINT signals from committed rh_status.json history: 632 min of NO-PUSH gaps (machine dead, hung, or unable to push) and 852 min DEGRADED (alive and pushing but unable to see or trade the account). The degraded figure was cross-checked against a completely independent source, laptop's rh_daemon.log: 892 from git vs 893 from the log on the same 09:30-16:00 clip. 

WINDOW SENSITIVITY, stated because it moves the answer a lot: on exchange hours 09:30-16:00 the same data gives 1884 min, 23.8%. The difference is designed idle time, not blindness, since the bot does not trade before 09:45 or after 15:55. Use the trading window. An earlier draft of this correction also counted Labor Day 2026-09-07 as a full trading day and reported 27.4%; that was a holiday bug in the measurement, not an outage. 

THE TAIL IS STILL THE RISK, and it is UNBOUNDED: two of the causes never self-heal. An expired CLI login (09-21) waits for a human, and a Modern Standby HANG (08-04, 09-22) leaves the machine unbooted until someone presses power; 09-22 waited 12 hours. Auto-logon covers a crash-and-restart (09-02) but cannot help a machine that never boots. laptop's SetThreadExecutionState fix removes the one factor common to all three crashes and is EVIDENCE-BASED, not proven; it is proven only by the absence of further Kernel-Power 41 events. 

HOW TO WEIGH IT: see question_being_answered. Under the BUNDLE reading this is a real property of Arm B and must not be corrected out. Under the STRATEGY reading it is a confound and must be. For an index arm with no stops the realised cost is delayed rebalancing and deposits sitting uninvested, which is small per minute; the design_principle argument holds, but the MAGNITUDE is ~20% of trading time, not ~11 min/session. Re-measure with this method, on this window, rather than assume the rate held.

UPDATE 2026-10-08 (cloud, at LAPTOP DAILY CHECK's request after the 2026-10-08 crash). THE METHOD IS NOW CODE: arm_b_downtime.py reproduces the published 852 degraded + 632 no-push EXACTLY (period 2026-08-24 to 2026-09-22 11:01 ET, 7476 trading minutes). The rule: a gap over 30 min between rh_status.json pushes is no-push; a shorter gap after a degraded snapshot is degraded; a degraded snapshot before a long gap covers its first 5 min; window 09:45-15:55 ET minus MARKET_HOLIDAYS. Run `python arm_b_downtime.py --episodes`; tests/test_arm_b_downtime.py pins every clause and the published figure. 

SAME RULE, 2026-09-22 11:01 to 2026-10-08 11:50 ET (newest snapshot, 12.1 sessions): 1016 degraded + 154 no-push = 1170 blind market-minutes = 26.1% of trading time, against 19.9% in the published window. CUMULATIVE 2026-08-24 to 2026-10-08 (32.3 sessions): 1868 degraded + 786 no-push = 2654 = 22.2%. The crash that prompted this: per LAPTOP DAILY CHECK's event log the laptop bugchecked (0x154 UNEXPECTED_STORE_EXCEPTION) and was down until 10:17 ET on 2026-10-08, which is 32 market-minutes inside the window by the pushes (09:45 to 10:17) and about 31 by laptop's log. 

TWO THINGS THE UPDATE SHOWS. (1) DEGRADED IS THE DOMINANT CAUSE: 1016 of the 1170 new minutes (87%), and six of the last twelve sessions end their degraded stretch at 14:41 or 14:42 ET (09-23, 09-24, 09-28, 09-30, 10-06, 10-07). That is a pattern in the history, not a diagnosis; the daemon log, not git, says why. (2) THE RULE SCORES HEARTBEAT SPACING AS DOWNTIME: the minutes between a session's last heartbeat (about 15:43 to 15:47) and the 15:55 close, and between 09:45 and the first push, count as no-push every night even when nothing is wrong: 169 of the published 632 and 119 of the 154 new. Without those edge minutes the published figure would read 1315 = 17.6% and the cumulative 2366 = 19.8%. They are NOT removed from the figures above, because the published number was computed with them; arm_b_downtime.py prints both. Which reading the November comparison uses is for laptop and Devon to decide (the window choice was already flagged as a judgement).

DECISION 2026-10-08 (Devon, asked by cloud; laptop and cloud both recommended it): the HEADLINE Arm B figure EXCLUDES the close/open edge minutes, and the figure with them is the stated upper bound. The daemon writes rh_status.json on every 60-second pass and only the PUSH is about every 15 minutes when healthy, so those minutes are a sampling artifact, not time Arm B could not act. To 2026-10-08 15:00 ET (32.9 sessions, 12155 trading minutes): HEADLINE 2366 blind market-minutes = 19.5%; UPPER BOUND 2654 = 21.8% (1868 degraded + 786 no-push, 288 of the no-push being edge minutes). The published window alone (to 2026-09-22 11:01) reads 1315 = 17.6% without edge minutes and 1484 = 19.9% with them (published as 19.8%). Since 2026-09-22 11:01: 1051 = 22.5% headline, 1170 = 25.0% with edge. Arm A's like-for-like figure is arm_A.downtime. 

WHAT THE NEW MINUTES ARE (laptop's event log and daemon log, 2026-10-08). (a) The six degraded stretches that end at 14:41 or 14:42 ET are ONE cause: the Claude session limit on the account the bridge shares with Devon's own sessions resets at 1:40pm CT (14:40 ET), and the daemon sleeps to the reset instead of retrying, so every exhaustion ends on the same wall-clock boundary. The STARTS vary and are the whole cost: the earlier in the session the quota runs out, the more of the day Arm B is blind (a limit hit at 14:09 ET cost about 30 minutes, at 13:05 about 95, at 11:11 about 210, at 10:52 about 230). It is quota headroom, not a code defect. (b) On 2026-10-08 the laptop went down twice: bugcheck 0x154 at 04:54 ET (no dump written; down until 10:17 ET; 32 market-minutes), and at 11:27 ET an unexpected shutdown with bugcheck code 0, up again at 11:32:52 with no human involved (about 5 market-minutes). 

RESOLUTION FLOOR: the method works from pushes, so it cannot see an outage that leaves a push gap of 30 minutes or less (heartbeats are about 15 minutes apart, so a shorter threshold would invent outages). Known miss: the 11:27 to 11:32 ET crash on 2026-10-08 (pushes at 11:13 then 11:33), about 5 market-minutes, so that day's true figure is about 37, not 32. A push-based measure under-reports: it missed the dominant case (degraded but pushing) once and the short tail once. From 2026-10-08 the daemon also emails Devon when it returns from an unannounced gap (rh_daemon.report_downtime), a second, push-independent record.

question_being_answered: DEFAULT READING: 'which strategy+platform BUNDLE should keep running?' The same number is correct under one reading and wrong under the other, so November must not leave this implicit (laptop, 2026-09-10). Under the BUNDLE reading, Arm B's laptop downtime is a genuine property of Arm B and correcting for it would be WRONG. Under a pure 'which STRATEGY is better' reading, where the winner would then move to the better platform, downtime IS a confound and MUST be corrected out. design_principle points at the bundle reading, which is why that is the default. DEVON SHOULD CONFIRM: if he intends the strategy question, the downtime correction becomes mandatory rather than optional, and arm_B.downtime_asymmetry changes from context into an adjustment.
